name: Replies make the structure move their turn calls for
purpose: A reply carries the structure its turn calls for and no more: a plain turn stays plain, a turn that calls for structure shows the problem, ideal, solution, alternatives, metric and milestone from the records first and the draft for what is missing, no existing record is duplicated, a metric value is only one the records hold, and at most one offer keeps the missing pieces.
record: Thirty-six written cases (evaluation/structure_in_conversation/build_cases.py) over neutral records, scored on the structured fields a turn emits and never on prose: six plain turns, four frames over bare records, three over held structure, two with nothing missing, three comparisons, five reviews, three focus turns, two declined offers, two held solutions and six over a quest that holds several solutions (the matched one keeps its own problem, ideal, metric with its value and milestone and gets no second metric; when none fits a new solution is proposed). One number: the share of cases whose move, parts, held or proposed state of each part, alternatives held and new, metric value shown, offer pieces and number of edits all equal what is expected. Weights are fixed before any arm is scored: every case counts once, and the share by kind shows where an arm is weak. Two advisory judged checks (the six terms used consistently, and the reply standing on its own for a newcomer) are built beside the arm and kept apart from this number.
disadvantages: The cases are written, and the move is given to the arm as the planner would emit it, so the number does not measure whether the move was classified right; that is measured on real turns by a replay. A name match decides that an alternative is already held. The judged checks share a model's bias and no real newcomer has read the replies.
cascading_conditionals: free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the arm and its rival were recorded on the same cases]
command: esoi run structure_in_conversation --impl none; esoi run structure_in_conversation --impl structure_move
